_note: Claims for elon-time.html, drawn by assets/home/claims.js. Field guide at the bottom.

sections.title: Full Self-Driving and autonomy
sections.intro: Musk has predicted full autonomy within roughly a year in almost every year since 2014; as of October 2026, Tesla still sells FSD to owners only as a supervised (Level 2) system, and Tesla’s Q3 2026 call moved unsupervised use in owners’ cars to Q2 2027, inside Robotaxi zones only ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/10/21/tesla-unsupervised-fsd-q2-2027-robotaxi-fleet/)).
notes: Entries through January 2026 follow [Wikipedia’s list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_predictions_for_autonomous_Tesla_vehicles_by_Elon_Musk), with Wikipedia’s own references as each entry’s source. Robotaxi entries from that list (Apr 2019, Apr 2020, Jan 2025, Jul 2025, Sep 2025, Jan 2026) are in the next section. Entries from November 2025 on, and outcomes after January 2026, are newer than Wikipedia’s list.

sections.title: Robotaxi and Cybercab
sections.intro: Musk promised over a million robotaxis by 2020; Tesla’s first paid rides came in June 2025 with a safety monitor aboard, and in October 2026 the service runs in about seven US metros, with only part of each fleet driverless and the Bay Area fully supervised ([Charge Port tracker](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)).

sections.title: Production and delivery guidance
sections.intro: Tesla’s big volume targets have mostly slipped: the 20-million-a-year goal for 2030 was dropped from company reports in 2024, deliveries fell in both 2024 and 2025 after growth was promised, and on the Q3 2026 call Musk’s target became about 5 million a year by around 2030 ([Not a Tesla App](https://www.notateslaapp.com/news/4867/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-call-recap-everything-you-need-to-know)).

sections.title: Product launch promises
sections.intro: Almost every new Tesla product shipped years after Musk’s date, often at a higher price or lower spec: the Semi (promised for 2019) reached high-volume production in Q3 2026, the Roadster (promised for 2020) is now targeted for 2028, and the $25,000 car became trimmed versions of the Model 3 and Y starting near $39,000.

sections.title: Financial and earnings claims
sections.intro: The best-documented false financial statement is the 2018 “funding secured” tweet, which a federal judge ruled false and reckless; other misses are profit forecasts and the claim that Teslas would rise in value.
notes: Forecasts here count only where Musk or Tesla named a specific result and date; broad valuation claims (for example that Tesla will be worth more than the next several companies combined) are left out because they cannot yet be checked.

sections.title: China and international claims
sections.intro: Musk’s misses abroad center on FSD approval: he has given at least four dates for full approval in China since 2024, and as of October 2026 regulators have still not granted it, while Tesla’s sales fell in China and BYD overtook Tesla globally in 2025.
notes: On sales: Tesla’s vehicle sales in China fell more than 16% year on year in Q1 2026 ([Automotive World](https://www.automotiveworld.com/?p=465578)), and BYD sold about 2.26 million EVs in 2025 against Tesla’s 1.64 million ([AFP via Prothom Alo](https://en.prothomalo.com/corporate/global/a0jkkus55a)). These are results rather than Musk statements; no sourced Musk forecast of Chinese unit sales was found to test against them.

sections.title: Optimus robot
sections.intro: Musk promised thousands of useful Optimus robots in Tesla factories in 2025 and sales to other companies in 2026; Tesla paused production in mid-2025 after building far fewer, only began “early production” in Q3 2026, and now says outside customers come around the end of 2027 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tesla-tsla-said-q3-earnings-000413028.html)).
notes: Broad claims such as Optimus making up 80% of Tesla’s value, or lifting Tesla to a $25 trillion market cap, are left out as not yet testable.

sections.title: Batteries, Dojo and other technology
sections.intro: Tesla’s in-house technology bets also ran behind Musk’s dates: the 4680 cell missed its 2022 volume target by a wide margin, and the Dojo supercomputer, pitched since 2019 as key to self-driving, was shut down in August 2025 weeks after Musk projected its next version at scale in 2026.

sections.title: Mars timelines
sections.intro: Musk has set a Mars date for nearly every two-year launch window since 2016, and none has been met: no SpaceX vehicle has gone to Mars, and in February 2026 he shifted SpaceX’s priority to a Moon city, saying Mars city-building would start in about 5 to 7 years ([Fox 9](https://www.fox9.com/news/musk-says-spacex-shifting-focus-self-growing-city-moon-before-mars-push)).
notes: The 2026 Mars window runs roughly November to December 2026, so these entries are marked from SpaceX’s own February 2026 change of plan rather than the window’s close.

sections.title: Starship, lunar tourism and reuse
sections.intro: SpaceX’s real achievements (booster landings, routine reuse, booster catches) came with dates that mostly slipped; the two announced private Moon flights never flew, and Starship reached orbit years after Musk’s 2022 target.

sections.title: Starlink and the IPO
sections.intro: Starlink became a large business but far smaller and later than SpaceX’s investor projections, and SpaceX went public in June 2026 despite Musk’s 2013 position that it would not list until its Mars ship was flying regularly.
notes: The 2015 and 2017 figures were company projections shown to investors and reported by the Wall Street Journal, not public statements by Musk; they are included because Reuters described them as targets set by Musk.

sections.title: Forecasts that came true
sections.intro: Four forecasts on [Wikipedia’s list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_predictions_for_autonomous_Tesla_vehicles_by_Elon_Musk) came true. They are kept apart from the misses above.

claims.claim: 90% of miles driven autonomously within three years
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: On-ramp to off-ramp on highways without touching the controls in under a year
claims.outcome: Autopilot (Oct 2015) handled highways but still needed the driver ([Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/cars/2015/10/driving-or-kind-of-not-driving-a-tesla-model-s-with-autopilot/))

claims.claim: Next year’s Tesla “90% capable of autopilot,” at least on highways
claims.outcome: Autopilot shipped Oct 2015 for highways, still supervised; Wikipedia counts it as partly met

claims.claim: Get in the car, go to sleep, wake at your destination, within about 10 years
claims.outcome: Not available to owners in 2026

claims.claim: A car capable of full autonomy in about three years
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Complete autonomy in about two years
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Summon your car from across the country within two years, charging itself on the way
claims.outcome: Never offered

claims.claim: Self-driving is “basically a solved problem”; complete autonomy less than two years away
claims.outcome: Tesla told the California DMV in 2020 that FSD would remain Level 2 ([flyingpenguin](https://www.flyingpenguin.com/technopuff-of-promises-broken-an-elon-musk-timeline/))

claims.claim: All new Teslas have the hardware for full self-driving
claims.outcome: Hardware 2 and 2.5 were swapped for Hardware 3; Musk said in Jan 2025 Hardware 3 cars need upgrading and in Apr 2026 that it cannot do unsupervised FSD (~4M cars) ([TechCrunch 2025](https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/30/elon-musk-reveals-elon-musk-was-wrong-about-full-self-driving), [TechCrunch 2026](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/22/elon-musk-admits-millions-of-tesla-owners-need-upgrades-for-true-full-self-driving/))

claims.claim: Fully autonomous LA-to-New York demo drive, no touches, by end of 2017
claims.outcome: Never done; Tesla’s Autopilot software director later testified the 2016 promo video was staged ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2023/01/17/tech/tesla-self-driving-video-staged/index.html))

claims.claim: Parking lot in California to parking lot in New York, no controls touched, by Nov or Dec 2017
claims.outcome: Never done

claims.claim: Drivers able to sleep at the wheel in about two years
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Coast-to-coast drive in three months, six at most
claims.outcome: Never done

claims.claim: Self-driving will cover all modes of driving by end of 2019
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Full self-driving “next year” as a generalized solution
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: “Feature complete” FSD this year, pickup to destination with no intervention: “I am certain of that”
claims.outcome: Did not happen; a 2021 DMV memo records a Tesla engineer saying Musk’s claims did not match engineering reality ([The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2021/05/07/tesla_engineer_autopilot/))

claims.claim: Cars with no steering wheel or pedals within two years
claims.outcome: Cybercab began slow production Apr 2026 ([CNET](https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/news/tesla-cybercab-begins-production/))

claims.claim: Basic Level 5 functionality complete this year
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: “Highly confident” the car will drive itself more reliably than a human this year
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Cameras and neural nets on par with or better than humans “this year”
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Full autonomy “does look like” it happens this year
claims.outcome: Did not happen; Dec 2023 recall covered ~2M cars over Autosteer ([flyingpenguin](https://www.flyingpenguin.com/technopuff-of-promises-broken-an-elon-musk-timeline/))

claims.claim: Level 4 or 5 later this year; better than human by year-end
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Other carmakers licensing FSD will become obvious this year
claims.outcome: No carmaker licensed FSD; in Nov 2025 Musk acknowledged none wanted to ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2025/12/04/elon-musk-tesla-fsd-drivers-can-now-text-drive/))

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD in Texas and California in 2025
claims.outcome: Not available to owners

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD to owners in California and other US regions in 2025
claims.outcome: Not available to owners

claims.claim: Sleep in your car and wake at your destination in many US cities by end of 2025
claims.outcome: Not available

claims.claim: Millions of Teslas operating fully autonomously in the second half of 2026
claims.outcome: Unsupervised driving only in Robotaxi fleets in about seven metros; owner use moved to Q2 2027 ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/10/21/tesla-unsupervised-fsd-q2-2027-robotaxi-fleet/))

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD “probably everywhere” in North America in 2026; most countries by end of 2026

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD for personal use in certain areas by end of 2025
claims.outcome: Not available; now Q2 2027

claims.claim: Owners can add or remove their car from the Tesla fleet “confidently next year”
claims.outcome: Moved to Q2 2027 on the Q3 2026 call ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/10/21/tesla-unsupervised-fsd-q2-2027-robotaxi-fleet/))

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD “a few months away”; FSD v14.3 would let you “pretty much fall asleep” and wake at your destination
claims.outcome: Not available to owners in Oct 2026

claims.claim: Consumer unsupervised FSD possible as early as Q4 2026; unsupervised operations in 10+ states by year-end
claims.outcome: Q3 2026 call moved consumer use to Q2 2027

claims.claim: Unsupervised FSD operating in “a dozen or so states” by end of 2026
claims.outcome: In Oct 2026, unsupervised rides only in Texas and Florida

claims.claim: Self-driving in wide release in the US by end of 2022
claims.outcome: FSD Beta (supervised) opened to all North American buyers in Nov 2022 ([CleanTechnica](https://cleantechnica.com/2022/11/28/tesla-full-self-driving-beta-goes-out-for-wide-release-in-north-america/))

claims.claim: Robotaxi launch tentatively Jun 22
claims.outcome: Launched Jun 22, with a safety monitor aboard ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/teslas-robotaxi-peppered-with-driving-mistakes-texas-tests-2025-06-25/))

claims.claim: First car to drive itself from factory to a customer’s home on Jun 28
claims.outcome: Done Jun 28, about 15 miles ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/30/tesla-sends-driverless-model-y-from-factory-to-customer-to-promote-its-robotaxi-tech/))

claims.claim: Cybercab production starts in April
claims.outcome: Began Apr 2026 at a rate Musk called “very slow” ([CNET](https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/news/tesla-cybercab-begins-production/))

claims.claim: “Very confident” of robotaxis next year; over a million on the road
claims.outcome: Zero robotaxis in 2020 ([The Drive](https://www.thedrive.com/news/38129/elon-musk-promised-1-million-tesla-robotaxis-by-the-end-of-2020-where-are-they))

claims.claim: Owners could earn up to about $30,000 a year renting their car as a robotaxi
claims.outcome: No owner has been able to add a car to the network as of Oct 2026

claims.claim: Robotaxi functionality “still looking good for this year,” pending regulators
claims.outcome: Did not happen

claims.claim: Dedicated robotaxi with no wheel or pedals in volume production in 2024
claims.outcome: Cybercab shown Oct 2024; production started slowly Apr 2026

claims.claim: Robotaxi rides will cost less than a subsidized bus ticket
claims.outcome: No evidence of bus-level fares

claims.claim: Cybercab for under $30,000, in production in 2026, before 2027
claims.outcome: Production began Apr 2026 at a “very slow” rate ([CNET](https://www.cnet.com/roadshow/news/tesla-cybercab-begins-production/)); on the Q3 2026 call Musk said Cybercab will mainly be Tesla-owned, with no consumer sale date ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/22/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))

claims.claim: Unsupervised paid robotaxi service in Austin in June, “no one in the car”
claims.outcome: Launched Jun 22, 2025 with a safety monitor in every car, invited riders only, small geofence ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/teslas-robotaxi-peppered-with-driving-mistakes-texas-tests-2025-06-25/))

claims.claim: Unsupervised service in California and other US areas in 2025
claims.outcome: California still requires a safety driver in every car in Oct 2026 ([Charge Port](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker))

claims.claim: Autonomous ride-hailing for about half the US population by end of 2025
claims.outcome: Austin plus a supervised Bay Area service

claims.claim: No safety drivers by end of 2025
claims.outcome: First monitor-free public rides Jan 22, 2026, a small number of cars in Austin ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/22/musk-says-tesla-takes-safety-supervisors-out-of-some-austin-robotaxis.html))

claims.claim: Robotaxis with no one in them in about three weeks
claims.outcome: About six weeks, in limited form

claims.claim: Seven new cities in H1 2026: Dallas, Houston, Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Las Vegas
claims.outcome: Dallas and Houston in April; Miami, Orlando and Tampa in July; Phoenix and Las Vegas still “coming soon” in Oct 2026 ([Tesla North](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-robotaxi-safety-report-four-new-cities/))

claims.claim: Fully autonomous vehicles across a quarter to half of the US and in dozens of major cities by end of 2026
claims.outcome: About seven metros in Oct 2026

claims.claim: 500,000 cars produced in 2018 (pulled forward from 2020)
claims.outcome: About 245,000 delivered in 2018; the goal was “virtually impossible” by spring ([Jalopnik](https://jalopnik.com/tesla-making-2-000-model-3s-per-week-musk-says-unders-1824253566))

claims.claim: 100,000–200,000 Model 3s built in H2 2017; 1 million total Teslas a year by 2020 ([Asymco](https://asymco.com/category/automotive))
claims.outcome: 222 Model 3s delivered in Q3 2017 and about 1,550 in Q4; about 500,000 total deliveries in 2020

numbers.metric: Model 3s in the second half of 2017
numbers.note: Low end of the 100,000–200,000 promised; actual is Q3 and Q4 deliveries added together

claims.claim: Model 3: 1,500 built in September and 20,000 a month by December 2017
claims.outcome: 260 built in all of Q3 2017 ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2018/07/01/tesla-5000-model-3-week-deadline))

claims.claim: 5,000 Model 3s a week by end of 2017; 10,000 a week some time in 2018
claims.outcome: 5,000 reached in the last week of June 2018, hours late, partly using a tent line; 10,000 a week never reached for Model 3 in 2018

claims.claim: 2,500 Model 3s a week by end of Q1 2018
claims.outcome: About 2,000 a week ([Jalopnik](https://jalopnik.com/tesla-making-2-000-model-3s-per-week-musk-says-unders-1824253566))

numbers.metric: Model 3s a week at the end of Q1 2018

claims.claim: About 50% average annual delivery growth for years; 20 million vehicles a year by 2030
claims.outcome: Dropped from Tesla’s impact report in May 2024 ([Reuters via Globe and Mail](https://theglobeandmail.com/world/video-tesla-drops-delivery-goal-of-20-million-vehicles)); now 5 million by ~2030

claims.claim: Tesla could build more than 1.5 million vehicles in 2022 ([Nasdaq/ETF Trends](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/tesla-looks-to-make-robotaxis-at-scale))

claims.claim: Cybertruck at roughly 250,000 a year some time in 2025 ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2023/10/18/elon-musk-warns-cybertruck-wont-be-profitable-until-2025/))
claims.outcome: About 17,000 delivered in 2025, by CleanTechnica’s estimate ([CleanTechnica](https://cleantechnica.com/2026/01/02/elon-musks-dramatic-miss-on-2025-tesla-cybertruck-sales/))

numbers.note: Promised as a yearly rate; actual is CleanTechnica’s estimate of 2025 deliveries

claims.claim: Vehicle volume growth of 20–30% in 2025 ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/?p=449253))
claims.outcome: Deliveries fell 8.5% to about 1.64 million, a second straight annual decline ([blue News](https://www.bluewin.ch/en/news/tesla-closes-a-year-with-a-decline-in-sales-for-the-first-time-musk-abandons-models-3071768.html))

claims.claim: Vehicle business will “return to growth in 2025”

claims.claim: Model X deliveries in 2014
claims.outcome: First deliveries Sep 2015 ([The Drive](https://www.thedrive.com/news/38129/elon-musk-promised-1-million-tesla-robotaxis-by-the-end-of-2020-where-are-they))

claims.claim: Model 3 starting at $35,000 before incentives
claims.outcome: Offered Feb 2019; moved “off menu” within weeks ([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2019/04/24/tesla-promise-35k-model-3-claims-few-ordering/)); ended for good Nov 2020 ([Carscoops](https://www.carscoops.com/2020/11/tesla-kills-off-the-35000-model-3-once-again/))

First trucks to PepsiCo Dec 2022; high-volume line started Q3 2026; production versions reported at ~$260,000–$300,000 ([Drive Tesla Canada](https://driveteslacanada.ca/semi/tesla-semi-high-volume-production/))

claims.outcome: Only supervised FSD, in two EU countries

claims.claim: Over a thousand, maybe a few thousand Optimus robots working at Tesla in 2025 ([Digital Trends](https://tech.yahoo.com/computing/articles/elon-musk-says-thousands-humanoid-010516986.html))
claims.outcome: Robots mostly moved batteries, at under half human efficiency; production paused mid-2025 ([Mezha](https://mezha.ua/en/news/virobnictvo-robotiv-tesla-optimus-stalo-na-pauzu-303129/amp/))

claims.claim: “Genuinely useful” robots in low production in 2025; high production for other companies in 2026 ([Digital Trends](https://www.digitaltrends.com/?p=3652284))
claims.outcome: No external sales in 2026; now expected end of 2027

claims.claim: At the We, Robot event, Musk presented Optimus robots serving drinks and chatting, saying they were not a canned video
claims.outcome: Bloomberg reported many interactions were remotely operated by staff; Musk did not say so on the webcast ([BNN Bloomberg](https://bnnbloomberg.ca/business/2024/10/14/teslas-optimus-robots-were-remotely-operated-at-cybercab-event))

claims.claim: About 5,000 Optimus built in 2025, later cut to 2,000
claims.outcome: Roughly 1,000 or fewer assembled before production and parts orders were halted for a redesign, largely over the hands ([TechSpot](https://www.techspot.com/news/109781-tesla-temporarily-halts-mass-production-optimus-robots-citing.html))

numbers.note: Target later cut to 2,000; actual is roughly 1,000 or fewer

claims.claim: Optimus V3 unveiled “probably in February or March 2026” ([Mike Kalil](https://mikekalil.com/blog/tesla-optimus-gen-3-delayed-again/))
claims.outcome: Delayed Mar 31 for “finishing touches,” then tied to a mid-2026 production start ([Not a Tesla App](https://notateslaapp.com/news/3884/tesla-delays-optimus-gen-3-unveil-for-finishing-touches))

claims.claim: 50,000–100,000 Optimus in 2026; a 1-million-a-year rate at Fremont by late 2026 ([Basenor](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-optimus-v3-reveal-set-for-late-july-what-we-know))
claims.outcome: “Early production” began Q3 2026; Musk now says reaching 20,000 a week will take about a year ([Not a Tesla App](https://www.notateslaapp.com/news/4867/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-call-recap-everything-you-need-to-know))

claims.claim: A million-mile battery pack in production next year
claims.outcome: No million-mile battery was unveiled at the Sep 2020 Battery Day ([Livewire](https://livewiremarkets.com/wires/tesla-battery-day-5-key-takeaways), [futurezone](https://futurezone.at/amp/produkte/11-dinge-die-elon-musk-fuer-2020-versprochen-hat/401160252))

claims.claim: 100 GWh of in-house 4680 cell capacity by 2022; 3 TWh by 2030 ([Electrive](https://www.electrive.com/2020/09/23/tesla-battery-day-tabless-4680-cell-and-in-house-production))
claims.outcome: Dry-coating the cathode stalled the ramp; by 2023 output covered about 50,000 vehicles a year ([Jalopnik via Yahoo](https://autos.yahoo.com/tesla-everyone-scrambling-perfect-next-160000444.html))

claims.claim: Battery advances would enable a $25,000 car within about three years
claims.outcome: See product launch promises: no $25,000 Tesla

claims.claim: Dojo would be the cornerstone of FSD training; Tesla would “double down” on it (Jul 2024)
claims.outcome: Team disbanded Aug 2025 ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/02/tesla-dojo-the-rise-and-fall-of-elon-musks-ai-supercomputer/))

claims.claim: Second Dojo cluster operating at scale in 2026
claims.outcome: Weeks later Musk called Dojo 2 “an evolutionary dead end” and shut it down ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/08/11/elon-musk-confirms-shutdown-of-tesla-dojo-an-evolutionary-dead-end))

claims.claim: People on Mars in about 10 years at best, 15–20 at worst ([Madhyamam](https://english.madhyamam.com/science/where-are-you-on-the-man-on-mars-mission-elon-musk-asked-1016585))
claims.outcome: No crewed Mars mission

claims.claim: Red Dragon to land on Mars in 2018; a mission every window after that; crew launch 2024, arrival 2025 ([SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/?p=60606))
claims.outcome: Red Dragon slipped to 2020, then was dropped in Jul 2017 ([Maciej Cegłowski](https://mceglowski.substack.com/p/musk-on-mars))

claims.claim: Two cargo ships to Mars in 2022, “not a typo”; first crew in 2024 ([CBC/Reuters](https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.4312878), [ScienceBlog](https://scienceblog.com/t-spacex-mars-deadlines-2016-2018-2022-2026-2028/))
claims.outcome: Starship’s first integrated test flight was Apr 2023

claims.claim: “Highly confident” of humans to Mars in 2026, maybe 2024; uncrewed vehicle in 2022 ([Cegłowski](https://mceglowski.substack.com/p/musk-on-mars))
claims.outcome: No uncrewed flight in 2022; no crewed flight planned for 2026

claims.claim: Would be surprised if humans were not on Mars within five years ([Space Explored](https://spaceexplored.com/2022/03/16/elon-musk-says-humans-will-be-on-mars-in-2029/))
claims.outcome: Three months later he said 2029

claims.claim: Humans on Mars in 2029 ([Futurism](https://futurism.com/the-byte/elon-musk-people-mars-landing-date))
claims.outcome: Mar 2025: 2029 possible, 2031 more likely ([Forbes Peru](https://forbes.pe/negocios/2025-03-16/musk-dice-que-quiere-enviar-un-cohete-a-marte-el-proximo-ano-y-con-misiones-humanas-a-partir-de-2029/))

claims.claim: About five uncrewed Starships to Mars in the 2026 window; crew in 2028 if they land safely ([Reuters via TradingView](https://es.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com,2024:newsml_L1N3L406N:0-spacex-plans-to-send-five-uncrewed-starships-to-mars-in-two-years-musk-says))
claims.outcome: In Feb 2026 SpaceX moved its priority to the Moon; no Mars launch is planned for the 2026 window ([Space Odyssey Hub](https://spaceodysseyhub.com/articles/spacex-starship-2026-mission-timeline))

claims.claim: 50–50 chance of an uncrewed Starship, carrying Optimus, leaving for Mars by end of 2026 ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/5/30/musk-says-50-50-chance-of-sending-uncrewed-starship-to-mars-by-late-2026))
claims.outcome: Same as above

claims.claim: Falcon Heavy debut within about two years
claims.outcome: First flight Feb 2018 after long delays ([SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/?p=60606))

claims.claim: Two paying private citizens on a week-long flight around the Moon in late 2018, on Falcon Heavy and Dragon ([Space.com](https://www.space.com/40805-spacex-delays-tourist-trip-around-moon.html))
claims.outcome: Delayed in 2018, then replaced by a Starship plan; never flew

claims.claim: dearMoon: Yusaku Maezawa and eight artists around the Moon on Starship in 2023
claims.outcome: Cancelled June 2024 because of Starship delays ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DearMoon_project))

claims.claim: Two orbital launches of the same Falcon 9 within 24 hours, “no later than next year” ([SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/?p=77346))
claims.outcome: Never done; booster turnaround remains days, not hours

claims.claim: Get Starship into orbit before the end of 2022 ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/elon-musk-says-world-still-needs-oil-gas-2022-08-29/))
claims.outcome: First integrated flight Apr 2023 failed within minutes; Starship first reached orbit in 2026 ([Space.com](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/starship-just-reached-orbit-for-the-1st-time-whats-next-for-the-spacex-megarocket))

claims.claim: SpaceX would attempt to catch a returning Starship upper stage “this month” ([Nerra Network](https://buttondown.com/patricknovak1/archive/spacex-ep070-starship-still-lacks-an-orbital-refuelin/))
claims.outcome: Not attempted; now planned for Flight 15 in November ([Northeast Times/Ars Technica](https://northeasttimes.com/2026/10/21/spacex-plans-to-catch-both-starship-stages-on-its-next-flight/))

claims.claim: Weekly Starship launches in H1 2027, twice weekly in H2 2027; ship-to-ship propellant transfer early 2027
claims.outcome: Ship-to-ship transfer not yet demonstrated after 14 flights

claims.claim: Investor deck: Starlink at 20 million subscribers, ~$12B revenue and ~$7B operating profit in 2022
claims.outcome: About 1.4 million subscribers and $1.4B revenue in 2022, per documents seen by the WSJ ([Reuters via Yahoo](https://sg.news.yahoo.com/spacexs-starlink-falls-short-growth-142430785.html))

claims.claim: Starlink at about 40 million subscribers and $30B revenue in 2025 ([Expansión](https://expansion.mx/tecnologia/2017/01/13/spacex-generara-75-mas-ingresos-que-tesla-para-2025))
claims.outcome: Bankers modeled total SpaceX revenue of about $15B for 2025 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/spacex-preparing-record-ipo-1-204259115.html))

numbers.note: Promised for Starlink alone; actual is bankers’ model for all of SpaceX

claims.claim: No SpaceX IPO until the Mars Colonial Transporter is “flying regularly”
claims.outcome: SpaceX listed on Jun 12, 2026, with no Mars flights ([Daily Ittefaq](https://en.ittefaq.com.bd/16930/spacex-set-for-wall-street-debut-in))

_fields.sections: Chapters of the file, in order: id, title, short (topic button), phrase (finishes “Musk had set N deadlines …” when the topic is picked), company, intro (one paragraph), notes (paragraphs shown after the entries). Text may use [label](url) links.
_fields.id: Unique slug; also the link anchor, e.g. elon-time.html#robotaxi-2019.
_fields.section: The id of the chapter this entry sits in.
_fields.company: Tesla or SpaceX. Each distinct value becomes a filter.
_fields.status: missed, late, partly, false, misleading, reversed, pending or kept (came true).
_fields.said: When he said it: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. saidLabel overrides the text shown (e.g. “2012–2019”).
_fields.claim: What he said, paraphrased unless in quotation marks. May use [label](url) links.
_fields.due: The deadline: YYYY means the end of that year, YYYY-MM the end of that month. null when there was none. dueLabel overrides the text shown (e.g. “~2023”).
_fields.delivered: When it happened, if it did. Leave null otherwise.
_fields.sources: List of { label, url } for where he said it.
_fields.numbers: Optional list of { metric, claimed, actual, prefix, suffix, approx, note }, drawn to scale as promised against actual.
